purpose: tx A ATTEMPT 1 — REVERTED. Banked as failure evidence per the stop-on-revert rule.
submittedBy: deployer, self-submitted — it is the named depositor here and deposits are public by design

shielded.note: the account key is in .env as MARKETS_DEMO_ACCOUNT_KEY, never committed

outcome.revertReason: Result::unwrap failed. — raised in the DEPLOYER's own __execute__ (class 0x061dac032f228abef9c6626f995015233097ae253a7f72d68552db02f2971b8f, selector __execute__), meaning an inner call reverted and the account unwrapped it
outcome.poolFeeNote: only ~2.54 STRK of GAS was taken, not the 6 STRK pool fee — collect_fee never ran, so apply_actions reverted before the pool charged anything

stateUnchanged.note: a reverted transaction changes nothing but the gas; verified by reading get_public_key and market_count back after the revert

leadingHypothesis: The v3 proof fields did not reach the sequencer. starknet.js Account.execute forwards proofFacts/proof to invokeFunction ONLY; prepareInvoke (which builds and signs) never sees them. Supplying resourceBounds to skip the fee estimate may also have changed the prepareInvoke path that carries them. apply_actions without a proof reverts, which matches a revert that charged gas but never reached collect_fee.
whatWasProvenBeforeSubmitting: the composed action list COMPILES — 42 span felts, 7 client actions
the hosted prover ACCEPTED and proved it (it refuses to prove reverting transactions, and did so twice earlier for SUBCHANNEL_NOT_FOUND)
so the action list itself is valid against the deployed pool; the failure is in submission, not composition
knownProductBug: apps/web/src/shell/submit.ts makeSelfSubmit has this same shape and has never run against mainnet. starknet.js Account.execute forwards proofFacts/proof to invokeFunction only, so the fee estimate simulates apply_actions unproven. Fixing it properly is post-deadline work; the evidence sequence routes through the relayer instead, which is the one proven path.

gasExhaustion.evidence: execution_resources l2_gas 78,047,360 consumed against a 100,000,000 bound — 22M units of headroom. Exhaustion charges AT the cap.

proofDroppedByStarknetJs.evidence: read from starknet.js@10.5.0 source: prepareInvoke returns hookedDetails unchanged when no account hook is registered (hookResult?.details ?? transactionsDetail), and execute spreads proofFacts/proof into invokeFunction. The pair survives and is broadcast.
proofDroppedByStarknetJs.methodWarning: getTransactionByHash shows NO proof_facts on this transaction — but it shows none on the SUCCESSFUL registration 0x4fbb either. The RPC does not echo proof fields at all. Project memory records this trap verbatim: "receipt-sampling can never verify proof presence." Do not re-derive proof presence from the chain; read the client source.

poolStateDrift.evidence: starknet_getEvents on the pool across blocks 13963369-13963388 (prove → execute) returns ZERO events and zero transactions. Pool state was identical at both ends.

proofExpiry.evidence: 19 blocks elapsed against a 450-block validity window.

traceIsExhausted: Two independent RPC hosts return the identical 685-character revert_reason, and its INNERMOST frame is still the deployer account (0x010fe91…, selector __execute__) with Result::unwrap failed. No pool frame appears at any depth, so the pool's own typed error — if there was one — is not recoverable from the chain.
stillUnexplained: A list the prover accepted (it refuses to prove reverting transactions), carrying its proof, with sufficient gas, against unchanged pool state, reverted on chain. Next step is the bare-deposit probe: the smallest proof-REQUIRING list, to establish whether this project can land any such transaction at all.
CAUSE_CONFIRMED: THE DEADLINE ARITHMETIC. `Markets::op_create` asserts `deadline - block_timestamp >= 900`; the script computed `deadline = now + 900` from its local clock, and proving plus inclusion pushed execution past the floor, so the contract panicked 'WINDOW_TOO_SHORT'. The pool unwraps the invoke's result, which is why a named felt surfaced as the generic Result::unwrap failed. Confirmed by the market-create attempt (0x404d7275…) reverting identically with the same 15-minute local-clock deadline, while every list WITHOUT an invoke landed.

supersededTheory.theory: an unmatched open note from `deposit({ amount })` with no recipient
supersededTheory.whyItLookedRight: the recipient-less form does declare an open note in the SDK's own swap example, and the UNDEPOSITED_OPEN_NOTES trap is genuinely invisible to compile_actions — so it fitted the evidence available at the time.
supersededTheory.whyItIsWrong: the market create used no deposit action at all — it spent a note — and reverted identically. The one thing both reverts shared was a deadline computed from local time.
supersededTheory.keptBecause: the trail is honest work; a theory that was reasonable and disproven is worth more on the record than a tidy file.
